title: It Is Well with My Soul
speaker: Lynn Baird
summary: Peace with God is what everyone is looking for. It comes because our sin, not in part but the whole, was nailed to the cross.
exhortation: Peace with God. That's what everybody in the world is looking for. It may be the main thing people are looking for. Paul calls it a peace that surpasses understanding in Philippians 4. In Romans 5 he says, "Since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." And Jesus himself says in John 14, "Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid."

Horatio Spafford wrote "It Is Well with My Soul" after his daughters were killed in a disaster at sea. In the first verse he writes, "When peace like a river attendeth my way, when sorrows like sea billows roll, whatever my lot, thou hast taught me to say, it is well, it is well with my soul." He had faced the worst disaster most of us can imagine. Life can be like that: peace one moment, and then disaster rolls in like sea billows. And yet God wants to give peace.

Where does that peace come from? In the third verse he writes, "My sin, oh, the bliss of this glorious thought! My sin, not in part but the whole, is nailed to the cross, and I bear it no more." In the face of that disaster, he was saying, "I had a much bigger problem. I was separated from God and not at peace with him. And God in his mercy took matters into his own hands and took my sin."

When Jesus was nailed to the cross, our sin was nailed to the cross. All of it, not just part of it. All the thoughts you thought no one knew about, God knew. All of that rebellion was nailed to the cross. And by faith in what Jesus did there, we have peace with God. You can have peace with God today. We don't have to carry that shame and guilt any longer. Through faith in Jesus Christ we come to God, and we have peace with him.
